description: Surface environment at Jezero crater, the Mars Sandbox v0.1 region. Primary sources are Perseverance MEDA (MY36 statistics derived in facts/derive/), Mastcam-Z, MOLA and the USGS HiRISE DTM. Superseded records are kept with superseded_by; nothing is a placeholder.

facts.label: Perseverance landing site (Octavia E. Butler Landing)
facts.notes: Jezero is a ~50 km crater on the NW rim of the Isidis basin; Noachian lake basin with a fluvial delta.

facts.label: Visible (880 nm) dust optical depth in the clear season, MY36

uncertainty.note: span of the published values: 0.4-0.5 over Ls ~20-135 (Bell et al. 2022), falling to ~0.25 in early northern summer and near 0.3 at the seasonal minimum before the Ls 153 storm (Lemmon et al. 2022); mornings run 0.05-0.2 higher from water-ice haze; neither paper states a numeric uncertainty, and the 10th/90th percentiles task F2 asked for are not published

facts.instrument: Perseverance Mastcam-Z solar imaging (880 nm), with Skycam and MEDA RDS calibrated to it

valid_for.season: MY36, Ls ~20-156 (sols ~20-313), clear season before the Jan 2022 storm

facts.notes: Replaces the placeholder. Bell et al. 2022 (Science Advances 8:eabo4856): "Over the first 275 sols (solar longitude Ls ∼ 20° to 135°, through about mid-Northern summer), observed 880-nm optical depths of 0.4 to 0.5 were consistent with seasonal expectations for dust" and "The early summer decline to an optical depth (τ) of ~0.25 mimics trends at other Mars landing sites at the same season". Lemmon et al. 2022 (GRL 49:e2022GL100126), section 3.2: "Prior to the storm, visible optical depth was near 0.3 and starting to increase from the seasonal minimum (Figure 1a)." and "In the next sols, visible optical depths were near 0.4, with IR values about half that, and the seasonal trend of slowly rising optical depth resumed." Surface irradiance ≈ TOA * exp(-tau/cos(sza)) * (scattering correction); the dusty season (Ls 150-300) runs higher and is covered by the storm record and the MCD scenarios (task F3). No archived tau series exists; see hypotheses.md 8b.

facts.label: Peak visible optical depth, regional dust storm 5-11 Jan 2022 (Ls 153-156)

uncertainty.note: abstract gives peak ∼2; section 3.2 gives RDS/TIRS peak 1.7 (visible) and 0.8 (9 µm); no numeric uncertainty stated

facts.instrument: Perseverance MEDA RDS and TIRS, with Mastcam-Z and Skycam (Lemmon et al. 2022, Figure 1a)
facts.notes: Lemmon et al. 2022, abstract: "Peak visible optical depth was ∼2, and visibility across the crater was briefly reduced." Section 3.1: "Unusual dust-lifting activity was noticed around the rover on sol 313 (LS 153.4°), and optical depths increased then, through sol 318 (LS 156.0°)." Section 3.2: "RDS and TIRS showed rapid excursions with factor-of-several changes and peak optical depths of 1.7 (visible) and 0.8 (IR)." A regional storm roughly quarters usable solar power for days. Global storms (2018 killed Opportunity) can reach tau ~8-10 and last months; none has been measured at Jezero yet.

facts.label: Dust devil frequency of occurrence (first 365 sols)
facts.notes: Peak 12:00-13:00 LTST. Dust devils at Jezero can exceed 100 m diameter. A dust devil damaged a MEDA wind sensor in the Jan 2022 storm. Relevant to solar panel dust loading (also cleaning events).

facts.label: Estimated GCR dose equivalent at Jezero

uncertainty.note: scaled from Gale measurement for ~1.9 km less atmospheric shielding and solar-cycle variation

facts.notes: Rule of thumb: ~1 m of regolith or ~2-3 m of water reduces GCR dose substantially; shielding is a design parameter, not a fact. Agent: model, do not state as measured.

facts.label: Likelihood of accessible water ice in the top 5 m at Jezero latitude (18 N)
facts.notes: SWIM maps show consistent shallow ice mostly poleward of ~35-40 deg latitude. Jezero is a science site, not a resource site. Water for a Jezero base is therefore hydrated minerals, atmospheric extraction, or import. This is a design constraint the agent must surface.

facts.label: Liquid water in fractured mid-crust (global inference from InSight)

uncertainty.note: single-site seismic inversion; authors argue it is likely global

facts.notes: Volume exceeds proposed ancient oceans. Not accessible with any plausible drilling; relevant to astrobiology scenarios, not to base water supply.

facts.label: Depth below which diurnal temperature swing is negligible

uncertainty.note: depends on thermal inertia; the annual wave penetrates several metres

facts.formula: skin depth d = sqrt(2*kappa/omega), kappa from thermal inertia and regolith density
facts.notes: Agent must compute this from the primitives library, not hard-code it. Buried or regolith-covered structures see the mean (~218 K), not the swing.
